That the sentence under the heading entitled “Transfer of Appropriations”, contained in title II of the First Supplemental Surplus Appropriation Rescission Act., 1946 (Public Law 301, Seventy-ninth Congress, approved
February 18, 1946), is hereby amended by striking out the period at the end of the sentence and inserting the following: “, and (3) the Missing Persons Act, approved March 7, 1942 (56 Stat. 143), as amended.”

fable.w: This section is a technical amendment that adds the Missing Persons Act to a transfer-of-appropriations provision. The only tempting cue is the word "Persons" in a statute's title, which is a proper noun and not an outside-party process. Nothing here provides for consultation, hearings, comment, rulemaking, advisory bodies, or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a previous statute regarding the transfer of appropriations. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It merely updates the list of acts referenced in a specific sentence.
qwen_block.s: That the sentence under the heading entitled “Transfer of Appropriations”, contained in title II of the First Supplemental Surplus Appropriation Rescission Act., 1946 (Public Law 301, Seventy-ninth Congress, approved February 18, 1946), is hereby amended by striking out the period at the end of the sentence and inserting the following: “, and (3) the Missing Persons Act, approved March 7, 1942 (56 Stat. 143), as amended.”

opus.w: This section only changes a sentence about transferring appropriations by adding a reference to the Missing Persons Act. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties or right to sue. Words like "approved" or the name of an Act are boilerplate and bring no one outside the federal government into a decision.
opus.s: is hereby amended by striking out the period at the end of the sentence and inserting the following: “, and (3) the Missing Persons Act, approved March 7, 1942 (56 Stat. 143), as amended.”
opus.b: The tempting reading would be to treat "Missing Persons Act" or the word "approved" as a sign of a process involving people outside the government. That fails because this section only makes a technical amendment to how appropriations can be transferred. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or allowed to comment.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a previous act regarding the transfer of appropriations. It adds the 'Missing Persons Act' to a list of acts for which funds can be transferred. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, advisory committees, consultation with outside entities, or rights to sue. It is purely an internal fiscal and legislative adjustment.
qwen_chat.s: That the sentence under the heading entitled “Transfer of Appropriations”, contained in title II of the First Supplemental Surplus Appropriation Rescission Act., 1946 (Public Law 301, Seventy-ninth Congress, approved February 18, 1946), is hereby amended by striking out the period at the end of the sentence and inserting the following: “, and (3) the Missing Persons Act, approved March 7, 1942 (56 Stat. 143), as amended.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a statute to include the "Missing Persons Act" implies some form of public involvement or consultation regarding missing persons. However, this is a purely legislative amendment to a list of acts for which appropriations can be transferred. It does not create any process for outside parties to consult with the government, comment on decisions, or participate in advisory bodies. The text is strictly about fiscal authority and statutory references.
